name: programbench_devset_10
purpose: Development and manual case-study set for the greenfield executable-test upper-bound experiment.

notes: The selected set intentionally approximates the original Rust-heavy language distribution.
Go is slightly overrepresented because yj, dsq, and jplot already have baseline/scaffold trajectories and are useful continuity cases.
C++ is omitted from the default set because the only easy C++ task found is json-tui, which has high TUI risk; it is kept as an alternate.

tasks.why: CLI behavior is concrete, hidden tests cover secret patterns, file traversal, errors, and output modes; we already have useful prior trajectory data.
tasks.risk: Many pattern/edge-case tests; sanitizer must avoid leaking original pattern tables if present outside eval tests.

tasks.why: Small-to-medium test suite with visible CLI/table-formatting behavior, good for manual inspection.
tasks.risk: Formatting tests may be brittle; exact alignment and style handling can dominate failures.

tasks.why: Manageable test count; focuses on CLI options, scaling, and deterministic text output.
tasks.risk: Rendering behavior may require careful golden-output handling.

tasks.why: Human-understandable command behavior around help, output, and conventional commits.
tasks.risk: May depend on realistic git/repository fixtures; sanitizer needs to preserve fixture layout.

tasks.why: Good CLI extraction/output-modifier task with enough tests to expose spec gaps.
tasks.risk: Regex/extraction edge cases may be broad; exact output conventions need inspection.

tasks.why: Already used in baseline/scaffold experiments; tests cover flags, errors, edge cases, ordering, and format conversion.
tasks.risk: Official branch tar contains original Go source; sanitized bundle must include eval tests and testdata only.

tasks.why: Strong previous oracle-spec signal; tests cover SQL behavior, input formats, stdin/file behavior, and error modes.
tasks.risk: A full implementation is broad; executable tests may strongly guide behavior but still leave implementation complexity.

tasks.why: Already included in prior experiments; tests cover CLI, spec parsing, stdin, terminal dimensions, and JSON processing.
tasks.risk: Terminal rendering and timeout/interval behavior can make evaluation slow or flaky on Mac.

tasks.why: Classic CLI with documentation-rich behavior; tests cover layout, errors, encoding, info, and font loading.
tasks.risk: Font-loading and encoding behavior may require many fixture files and exact formatting.

tasks.why: Good C CLI case with input/output, errors, and image fixtures; more human-inspectable than TUI-like C tasks.
tasks.risk: Image dependencies and golden output comparisons may be harder to satisfy in a greenfield implementation.

alternates.reason: Use if we need one C++ task for distribution fidelity; default-excluded due TUI risk.
Good Go alternate if jplot is too slow/flaky.
Good Rust alternate, but ELF-format behavior may be less immediately inspectable.
